title: With wisdom
hook: invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good counsel, and argue in the best way (16:125)

segments.voice: Yesterday: justice, excellence and giving to kin, the verse the Friday sermon comes home to. And a week ends.

Somewhere right now a comment thread about religion has gone on for two hundred replies. Nobody in it has changed their mind. Everyone in it has gotten a little meaner. Near the end of An-Nahl there's a verse about exactly this: how to talk about faith with people who don't share yours, or don't share your reading of it. It doesn't tell anyone to stay quiet. It tells them how to speak, and names three tools.

Pickthall's translation of 16:125: "Call unto the way of thy Lord with wisdom and fair exhortation, and reason with them in the better way." Tool one: hikmah, wisdom. The root h-k-m has to do with holding something firm and judging well; the classical dictionaries list, from the same root, hakamah, the part of a horse's bridle that steers and restrains. Wisdom, in that picture, is knowing when to pull back: the right thing at the right time to the right person, or nothing yet. Tool two: al-maw'izah al-hasanah, good counsel, the kind that comes from someone who obviously cares about you. Tool three is the surprising one. Jadil: argue, debate. The verse doesn't forbid arguing. It says argue billati hiya ahsan, in the way that is best. Ahsan shares a root with ihsan from yesterday: excellence, doing something beautifully. So even a disagreement is supposed to be done well. Then the verse ends with a sentence that lowers the temperature of every argument: your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best who is guided. In the verse's terms, the speaker answers for the manner; the outcome is God's. Another verse, 29:46, makes the same point about the People of the Book: don't argue with them except in the best way. This week's verses were gifts: countless favors, milk from between, the bee, justice and excellence. Today the gifts turn into a way of talking: wise, kind, and, when it comes to arguing, beautiful.
screen: `HIKMAH: THE BRIDLE THAT STEERS.` · `GOOD COUNSEL, FROM SOMEONE WHO CARES.` · `ARGUE, BUT IN THE BEST WAY.` · `HE KNOWS BEST; THE RESULT ISN'T YOURS.` · then, large: `REASON WITH THEM IN THE BETTER WAY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a disagreement you're in right now, about faith, politics, or whose turn it is to do the dishes, and picture the other person's face. Slowly find the strongest version of their point, the one they'd be glad to hear you say, then picture saying your own view in a way they could hear without bracing. Don't plan to win; plan to speak well.
Hikmah. Wisdom, from a root about holding firm and judging well: the first tool for speaking about faith, before counsel and before argument. Today's word.
Your line: argue in the best way. The outcome isn't yours to hold. Day four hundred fifty-five, and a week complete.

howItsDone: Muslim teachers cite 16:125 as the guiding verse for da'wah, inviting others to Islam, and for interfaith conversation; many emphasize gentle speech and leaving guidance to God.

fork.setup: a friend mocks your faith in front of others, and you know you could win the argument. 16:125 has three tools. which comes first in the verse?
fork.reveal: wisdom comes first, then good counsel, then argument in the best way. and the verse ends by leaving the outcome to God.

original.note: Arabic: wisdom, from the root h-k-m, to hold firm and to judge.

trapdoor: what you thought: be wise when you talk about religion.
what it means: three tools in order, wisdom, good counsel, and argument done in the best way, with the result left to God.
what a scholar hears: h-k-m gives hakamah, part of a horse's bridle; ahsan in 'the better way' echoes ihsan in 16:90.

chat.says: How does the Qur'an say to talk about faith with people who disagree?
options: With wisdom and good counsel, and if you argue, argue in the way that is best.
Never discuss it at all; the Qur'an tells believers to stay silent.
Argue hard until they agree, since the outcome rests on you alone.
chat.meaning: 16:125: call with wisdom and fair exhortation, and reason in the better way. God knows best who is guided; the outcome is His.
